claim: States what the body is doing, and it is the spine of the i2v motion prompt as well as the pose in the still. A director sets it because walking, running and sprinting are three different stories about how urgent this is.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: relaxed stance, shifting weight, idle pose
sprinting, full sprint, deep forward lean, legs extended
standing up, rising from a crouch, pushing off the ground
sitting down, lowering into a seat, bending knees
falling, mid-air, arms out, off balance

review.issue: still ("standing still, motionless, static pose") and idle ("relaxed stance, shifting weight, idle pose") cannot differ in a single frame — "shifting weight" is a description of motion over time, and both resolve to a boy standing. The card is correctly renderable overall, but these two panels will be the same image.
review.fix: Either merge them for the still card and note that the still/idle distinction exists only in the LTX motion prompt, or make idle a genuinely different held pose — "contrapposto, weight on one leg, hands loose at sides" — and accept it now overlaps char.posture.leaning.
